subject: Cognitive Science
title: Abstract Concepts
description: A quick, practical guide to Abstract Concepts.

hook.text: You can point to a chair, but can you point to "justice"? Some concepts have no physical form.

buildup.text: Abstract concepts like freedom, time, and truth cannot be seen, touched, or tasted.

discovery.text: Brain imaging shows abstract concepts activate language regions more than concrete ones do.

twist.text: Yet we often ground them in bodily metaphors. The future is "ahead," sadness is "down."

climax.text: Abstract thought may piggyback on the same circuits that handle physical experience.

punchline.text: Even ideas without bodies live in the body.

quiz.question: What brain regions do abstract concepts especially activate?
